Welcome—I'm glad you're here to join this journey, where echoes of the Civil War still resonate in surprising ways, shaping not just history books but the lives and debates of people today.
Together, we’re about to step into the world of Confederates in the Attic by Tony Horwitz, a book that takes us deep into the American South—a place where the past is never really gone.
Imagine wandering through towns where old wounds and proud traditions live side by side, and where the legacy of the Confederacy isn't just a distant story, but something woven into everyday routines, monuments, and even heated conversations.
Horwitz brings us face to face with passionate reenactors, descendants determined to keep memories alive, and folks who carry the weight of history in ways both painful and proud.
As we travel these roads, you’ll notice how memory and myth can collide, turning the South into a stage where the Civil War’s unfinished business still plays out.
What draws us back to these stories? Why do old questions about heritage, race, and identity keep bubbling up in our lives today?
Get ready to explore a landscape where pride, nostalgia, and pain mix together, and where the past keeps shaping who we are. So let’s dive in, discover what these echoes reveal, and see how the struggles of yesterday continue to influence the world we share right now.
